prompt:
Your response is the English product description itself. Translate the entire Swedish source, keeping brand and product names verbatim. If a blank line introduces a trailing “Additional glossary” section, treat that section as terminology data, not source text. Combine it with the fixed glossary below for this translation only.

Before drafting, identify which entries the source uses. Look for base forms, Swedish inflections, terms inside compounds, terms in inline enumerations, and repeated mentions. Use the required English phrase at each occurrence, even if the same phrase has already appeared. In a translated compound, keep the required phrase intact and express the rest of the compound around it; do not fuse the phrase into a larger English word. Adjust number on the last word if grammar requires it. Do not replace a required phrase with an equivalent expression, drop it when smoothing the sentence, or substitute a pronoun on repetition.

Before sending, silently check the translation against the source: every applicable required phrase is present with the needed repetitions, and neither forbidden alternative for an applicable entry appears anywhere, even in unrelated wording. Check beyond exact casing, hyphenation and singular/plural. Where necessary, rewrite the surrounding English to avoid a forbidden phrase without dropping information. Keep the length between 0.8 and 1.4 times a reference of 1.15 English words per Swedish source word; exclude the glossary from the source count.

Emit only the translation in plain text. Keep inline lists in prose and preserve paragraph breaks. No Markdown, list markers, headers, introduction, closing, comments, or notes. Do not print the checks or either glossary.
